hook: You can't bolt agents onto your platform and call it AI strategy. If agents choose your SDKs and patterns, your docs and MCP surfaces are now architecture.
angle: Use Microsoft's AX Practitioner Playbook plus the enterprise extension of GitHub Spec Kit to argue that the knowledge sources agents consume — docs, samples, templates, MCP configs — are governed platform assets. Frame it as a quality-and-change-control problem, not a docs chore, and explain how governed catalogs keep agentic delivery consistent across many teams.

hook: MCP is quietly becoming the connective tissue between agents — and its trust model is a structural risk, not a bug.
angle: Turn the Ars Technica MCP report and Nadella's 'assume the model is compromised' framing into an architect's checklist: agent identity, egress control, prompt provenance, and blast-radius limits for any multi-agent system touching regulated data. Pair it with GitHub's open-source security agent as the inspectable-automation counterexample.

hook: As agents write more code, secret sprawl scales with it. Push protection isn't a courtesy check anymore — it's a pipeline control.
angle: Use GitHub's 'secret protection must scale with software' argument plus ReviewBench to make the case that AI-accelerated delivery needs centrally enforced security controls and measurable AI review. Connect it to why regulated change-control wants evidence and version control, not vendor promises.

hook: Data residency isn't a cloud-exit story. GA of SQL Server on Azure Local means you can modernize where the data already lives.
angle: For healthcare and finance clients, frame SQL Server on Azure Local plus FabCon's governed-data messaging as a modernization path that respects residency and sovereignty constraints without a forced lift-and-shift. Be explicit that residency support is a consideration to validate, not a compliance guarantee.

hook: A universal bank deploying frontier models at scale is a better governance case study than any vendor whitepaper.
angle: Use Barclays' expanded Anthropic collaboration to discuss what makes regulated AI adoption defensible: evaluation harnesses, access governance, and human oversight. Anchor it in architecture decisions an Azure solution architect actually owns, and keep compliance claims framed as considerations.
